snippet.title: Geoeconomics Revisited: Josh Lipsky and Matteo Maggiori
snippet.description:
As global powers face rising geopolitical tensions, sanctions, export controls, and tariffs are once again tools of leverage, marking the resurgence of geoeconomics, where economic policy and national security converge. This approach to business was largely abandoned by the West after the Cold War, though for most other countries, geopolitics and economics have always been closely linked. Josh Lipsky is the founding director of the GeoEconomics Center at the Atlantic Council, and Matteo Maggiori is a professor of finance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business. In this podcast, they discuss the new face of geoeconomics and its seemingly vengeful comeback.

snippet.title: The Russian Bolshevik Revolution (1917) [Parts 1-2]
snippet.description:
How did Lenin defy Classical Marxist understanding and bring socialism to the primarily-peasant Russian Empire? In this series, we explore both how Lenin theoretically planned to organize a Bolshevik movement in the extremely-unpromising environment of Czarist Russia, and also how those plans were executed and adjusted in reality amidst the political turbulence of 1917.

This is the completed version of the previous 2-part series:
1. Lenin's Strategy: https://youtu.be/11GEbYbRTAQ
2. Mar-Nov 1917: https://youtu.be/S0fOT3EATag

SCRIPT: https://strategosstuff.blogspot.com/search/label/The%20Russian%20Bolshevik%20Revolution

All interpretations and errors are my own.
